Hi Erin / Kamal —

Thanks — happy to kick this off. I attached a concise ramp verification playcard and a loadscript template to make the runs repeatable from your side. High level answers below; the playcard has the step-by-step checklist we usually follow.

Acceptance targets (initial):
- 95th percentile latency: <= 350ms average (for typical user queries)
- P99 latency: <= 1.1s (tail target during steady-state)
- Sustained throughput: scale to 1,000 qps with <15% increase in average latency vs baseline at 200 qps
- Error rate: <0.5% 4xx/5xx during ramp and steady windows

Recommended test plan (summary):
1) Baseline capture (10m, single-user ramp) — validate instrumentation
2) Step ramps: 100 -> 250 -> 500 -> 750 -> 1000 qps (10m per step, 5m cool-down)
3) Spike tests: 2x short spikes at 2,000 qps for 60s to validate graceful degradation/fallbacks
4) Long tail verification: 60m steady at target qps with KV cache warmed

Artifacts we need from you: raw telemetry export (CSV), per-request latency histograms, and the loadscript you used. We’ll run the same script from our side to cross-validate.

Operational roles:
- NovaGrid: provide test credentials, coordinate AWS test IAM/region, run their loadscript and upload telemetry.
- Redwood (Monica & Ben): own cluster-side runs, isolation checks, and produce the ramp_results_template.xlsx with evidence.
- CS (Priyom): observer for acceptance sign-off and schedule liaison.

I put Monica and Ben on this thread so they can confirm the run windows and any infra prep. I’ll also carve out a 60-minute sync slot on Feb 19 to walk through the playcard.

Attachments: ramp_verification_playcard.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB), loadscript_template.json (json, 12KB)

—
Naomi Feldman

Team —

Following up on Erin’s note. Please see the proposed ops matrix below; I need confirmation on ownership and any gating items before Feb 19 sync.

Ops matrix (short):
- Redwood staging endpoint: us-west-2 staging cluster (dedicated namespace) — owner: Ben
- Test harness: k6-based distributed driver (we’ll accept your k6 script or use loadscript_template.json) — owner: Monica
- Telemetry collection: Prometheus + per-request JSON export; we need a CSV of raw spans for cross-correlation — owner: Monica
- KV cache warm strategy: pre-seed using 30m warm job prior to step ramps — owner: Ben
- Post-run evidence pack: ramp_results_template.xlsx + zipped telemetry + client-side loadscript — owner: Ben/Monica

Specific asks:
1) Ben — confirm node counts we should spin to guarantee the 1,000 qps target while keeping single-request latencies consistent. If you need a dry run, suggest Feb 18 morning.
2) Monica — confirm we have a script to extract P95/P99 histograms in the format in the playcard. If not, we can provide a small python utility.
3) Priyom — please draft the acceptance sign-off checklist and a one-paragraph customer-facing summary for the Feb 20 run.

Risks to call out: cold-cache tail latency, regional egress limits on their account, and variability from tokenization differences (they use mixed-length prompts). If we see >2x P99 vs baseline, we’ll auto-trigger a mitigation run to collect deeper traces.

I’ll schedule the Feb 19 walkthrough and add our shared drive link for artifacts.

Thanks — Naomi
